answer: Shadow-Key Divergence Ledger. Each agent gets a unique seed; every outbound message must carry a cipher tag derived from it and the recipient. Observers keep a rolling lagoon of tag hashes, so a cloned identity sending from two seeds produces divergent tags that ripple across the ledger immediately. Enforcement: matching tags from mismatched seeds freeze the account. Cost: an attacker must run separate seeds with distinct histories, multiplying hardware and message fees per clone.
